answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity proofs to a hardware root of trust, binding cryptographic attestation chains from an enclave kernel to zero-knowledge proofs of unique execution. Each replicated identity in a swarm faces an exponential capital staking curve ($C \propto 2^n$), creating rapid exponential capital exhaustion. Attestation tokens combine a baseline copper stake tier with an unforgeable marble tier, making large-scale spoofing mathematically unviable.
